title: Brownfield grant and council pay review
subtitle: Winter snow and salt response, Age Friendly award, youth jobs delegation, Cowan reserve fund, AI education session
overview: Council approved a brownfield tax-increment grant for 161 Ottawa Street South, capped at $62,960, in exchange for a filed Record of Site Condition. It also approved a reserve fund for the Cowan Recreation Centre and directed staff to hire a consultant to review council remuneration, with any changes taking effect for the 2026-2030 term. {{vote:m7}}

After an in camera session, council directed the Chief Administrative Officer to take revised terms into account on a potential land acquisition, using authority granted in May 2025. The minutes do not describe the property or terms.

Council heard a walk-in delegation asking the City to expand paid summer jobs for youth. It also marked the City's provincial Age Friendly Community recognition and began Black History Month. During questions, staff agreed to bring an information report on winter maintenance and snow removal by the end of June 2026. The Mayor said a regional water supply update is expected in the next meeting cycle.

decisions.detail: Council approved a tax-increment grant of up to $62,960 for the owners, for up to 10 years, in exchange for a filed Record of Site Condition {{vote:m4}}.
Council approved the reserve fund as set out in the reserve information sheet attached to the staff report {{vote:m3}}.
Staff will engage a consultant for a scoped review of council remuneration, with changes effective for the 2026-2030 term, and update policy GOV-COU-020 as part of it {{vote:m7}}.
Following an in camera meeting, council directed the Chief Administrative Officer to account for revised terms when using the authority granted in May 2025 {{vote:m6}}.
Council received the staff report on the artificial intelligence education session as information {{vote:m5}}.

debate: A delegate urged the City to expand paid summer jobs and experience opportunities for youth, citing difficulty finding work and concern about rising homelessness and reliance on food banks.
In response, the Mayor said the City already offers summer work for students, noting a recent job fair that drew a large turnout, and encouraged the delegate to look at federal summer job programs.

One councillor praised staff for work during a record-snowfall winter and asked for an information report on lessons learned; staff said it would cover service levels, surge capacity, the road salt contract, technology and communications.

Asked about salt supply, staff said provincial demand rose after an early winter, so the City is using sand-salt mixes on more roads, working with its supplier on deliveries, and expects to need salt into spring as snow melts.
